description: Examinations dated on either end date are counted together with those dated in between.

d.request: Average of non-NULL `ANA` and total row count for Examination rows where `Examination Date` text is between '1995-11-09' and '1997-03-17' inclusive, returned as one row with the unrounded average first and the count second.
d.sql: SELECT AVG(ANA), COUNT(*) FROM Examination WHERE `Examination Date` BETWEEN '1995-11-09' AND '1997-03-17'

a.request: Looking at examinations with an `Examination Date` on or after 1995-11-09 and on or before 1997-03-17 (comparing the dates as text), what is the average `ANA` value (ignoring missing values) and how many examination records are there in total? Give the answer as a single row with the unrounded average first and the record count second.
a.sql: SELECT AVG(ANA) AS avg_ana, COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM Examination WHERE `Examination Date` >= '1995-11-09' AND `Examination Date` <= '1997-03-17';

c.request: For examinations held between 1995-11-09 and 1997-03-17 (comparing the `Examination Date` as text), what is the average `ANA` value (ignoring missing values) and how many examination records are there in total? Give one row with the unrounded average first and the record count second. Examinations dated on either end date are counted together with those dated in between.
c.sql: SELECT AVG(ANA) AS average_ana, COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM Examination WHERE `Examination Date` BETWEEN '1995-11-09' AND '1997-03-17';

b.request: Examinations with `Examination Date` BETWEEN '1995-11-09' AND '1997-03-17' (inclusive of both endpoints, compared as text): the average of non-NULL `ANA` values (AVG ignores NULLs, unrounded) and the total count of all matching rows (COUNT(*)), returned as one row with average first and count second.
b.sql: SELECT AVG(ANA), COUNT(*) FROM Examination WHERE `Examination Date` BETWEEN '1995-11-09' AND '1997-03-17';
b.raw: Examinations with `Examination Date` BETWEEN '1995-11-09' AND '1997-03-17' (inclusive of both endpoints, compared as text): the average of non-NULL `ANA` values (AVG ignores NULLs, unrounded) and the total count of all matching rows (COUNT(*)), returned as one row with average first and count second.
